subject: Committed spend tranche sweep — operational playbook & model
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T15:23:00Z
Subject: Committed spend tranche sweep — operational playbook & model

Emma — great talking earlier. Per our call, attaching a working model and a short operational playbook for a tranche-based prepay wallet that lets Acme ramp consumption while preserving a multi-year discount structure. High level: 

- Structure: Annual committed envelope split into 12 monthly tranches (sweep) with a 30% frontloaded option for Year 1 to help burst scenarios.
- Discounts: Year 1 prepay -> 12% discount on list; Year 2 (if prepaid at signing) -> 6%; acceleration credits if monthly drawdown exceeds forecast by >20%.
- True-up: Quarterly true-up where actual usage is reconciled against tranches; overconsumption draws from buffer or triggers top-up invoice.
- Invoicing: Monthly sweep invoice for scheduled tranche; separate true-up invoice at quarter close.
- Shelf buffer: 8% of annual commitment held as buffer to prevent immediate top-ups for short spikes.

Attached: "20260915-commit-tranche-model.xlsx" (scenario tabs: baseline, frontload, accelerated usage) and a draft SOW. Key asks from Acme to confirm so we can finalize pricing: 
1) preferred frontload % (0 / 30 / 50)
2) accounting preference (invoice upfront vs monthly sweep)
3) whether procurement needs a PO before DocuSign.

If you prefer, we can propose an alternate milestone-triggered drawdown (monthly tranches tied to usage milestones) — this reduces prepay exposure for you but complicates billing. Happy to walk through the model on a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-09-11T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Committed spend tranche sweep — operational playbook & model

Stephanie — thanks for this and for the clear model. A few clarifying Qs from my side and procurement: 

- Can you summarize how the quarterly true-up interacts with our existing vendor payment terms? If we prepay Year 1 at signing, will the true-up generate credits or additional invoices?
- For the acceleration credits: are those applied immediately to our wallet or reflected as a rebate on the following invoice?
- We prefer minimal surprise invoice timing — will you commit to 15 business days’ notice ahead of any additional top-up?
- Procurement asked whether the shelf buffer can be reduced to 5% if we commit to a 24-month term instead of 12.

I looped in procurement (procurement@acme.com) — they’ll want the SOW and the payment schedule in a format they can attach to the PO. Can we also get a DocuSign-ready SOW and a split invoice schedule?

Also, can we schedule a short call next week to run through the model with the billing team? Availability: Tue/Wed mornings PST.

—Emma
Emma Jones
Head of AI Platforms
Acme Cloud
emma.jones@acme.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Committed spend tranche sweep — operational playbook & model

Stephanie / Dev — reviewed Emma’s questions and the model. My recommendation to present tomorrow: 

- Offer options: (A) 12% Year1 prepay with 8% shelf buffer (standard); (B) 10% Year1 / 5% Year2 with buffer reducible to 5% for a 24-month commit. Clearly list cashflow implications in the SOW to make procurement’s job easier.
- True-up mechanics: implement as quarter-close reconciliation. If usage > committed tranches, consumption first eats buffer; remaining overage -> invoice next monthly sweep. If usage < committed, credit is applied to the subsequent month’s tranche (not refundable). 
- Acceleration credits: apply immediately to the wallet as an add-on token credit so it’s visible in the console (preferred for transparency).
- Contracting: Legal will permit a DocuSign SOW and a one-page payment schedule attachment for the PO. Avoid multi-line complex amortization tables in Procurement-facing materials.

I’ll prepare a short negotiation checklist and a one-page comparison (A vs B) for the call. Also suggest we prepare a fallback: milestone-triggered drawdown (usage bands) if procurement pushes back on large prepay.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
